## SCHOLARLY + DS&A CONTEXT
# ALGORITHM: Mantel-Haenszel DIF
#   source:      journey-os-algorithms-scholarly.html §IX
#   complexity:  time O(n*k*s) where n=students, k=items, s=score strata · space O(s)
#   parameters:
#     - alpha_MH = sum(Aj * Dj / Tj) / sum(Bj * Cj / Tj) across score strata j
#     - MH D-DIF = -2.35 * ln(alpha_MH)
#     - ETS classification:
#       A (negligible): |MH D-DIF| < 1.0
#       B (moderate):   1.0 <= |MH D-DIF| <= 1.5
#       C (large):      |MH D-DIF| > 1.5
#     - minimum sample: >= 50 students total (>= 25 per group)
#     - score stratification: by total score quintiles
#   security:    FERPA — demographic group membership is sensitive
#   invariants:
#     - DIF not computed if either group has < 25 students (returns null with reason)
#     - Category C items automatically flagged for faculty review
#     - Demographic data never exposed in API response — only DIF category
#     - MH D-DIF sign indicates direction: positive = favors reference, negative = favors focal
#
# FOUNDATION: Holland & Thayer, 1988
#   claim:   MH procedure detects uniform DIF (consistent across ability levels)
#   rule:    Stratify by total score to control for ability differences
#   applies: features/analytics/services/DifService.ts → computeMHDIF()

## Summary
Implement Mantel-Haenszel Differential Item Functioning (DIF) detection to identify assessment items that perform differently across demographic groups, with ETS A/B/C classification and automatic equity flags.

## User story
As an assessment director, I want to identify items that function differently across demographic groups (DIF), so that I can review flagged items for potential bias and ensure equitable assessment for all students.

## Why this matters
DIF-flagged items may indicate bias in assessment content. Without DIF analysis, biased items silently disadvantage specific student groups. This is both an LCME accreditation requirement (equitable assessment) and a FERPA-sensitive operation (demographic data must be protected). Incorrect stratification or classification thresholds would either miss biased items or flag too many items unnecessarily.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DifService.computeMHDIF() implements Mantel-Haenszel statistic with score stratification by quintiles
- [ ] MH D-DIF computed as -2.35 * ln(alpha_MH) per ETS specification
- [ ] ETS classification applied: A (|D-DIF| < 1.0), B (1.0-1.5), C (> 1.5)
- [ ] Returns null with reason when either demographic group has < 25 students
- [ ] Category C items automatically flagged with "equity_review_required"
- [ ] EquityPanel displays: DIF category per item (A/B/C badges), count of flagged items, no raw demographic data
- [ ] FERPA compliance: demographic group membership NEVER included in API response — only DIF category and direction
- [ ] EquityPanel integrates into ItemAnalyticsDashboard
- [ ] Unit tests verify computation against published example from Holland & Thayer

## Schema changes
```sql
-- DIF analysis results
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS item_dif_analysis (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  assessment_item_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES assessment_items(id),
  exam_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES exams(id),
  comparison_groups TEXT NOT NULL, -- e.g., 'gender', 'ethnicity' (category only, not values)
  alpha_mh NUMERIC(8,4),
  mh_d_dif NUMERIC(6,3),
  dif_category CHAR(1) NOT NULL CHECK (dif_category IN ('A', 'B', 'C')),
  dif_direction TEXT CHECK (dif_direction IN ('favors_reference', 'favors_focal', 'none')),
  n_reference INTEGER NOT NULL,
  n_focal INTEGER NOT NULL,
  flags TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  reason TEXT,
  computed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  institution_id UUID NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE(assessment_item_id, exam_id, comparison_groups)
);

ALTER TABLE item_dif_analysis ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "Faculty and admin read item_dif_analysis"
  ON item_dif_analysis FOR SELECT
  USING (institution_id = auth.jwt() ->> 'institution_id');
```

## Code patterns to follow
```typescript
// Pattern: FERPA-safe DIF computation
// features/analytics/services/DifService.ts

export class DifService {
  static readonly MIN_GROUP_SIZE = 25;
  static readonly DIF_THRESHOLDS = { A: 1.0, B: 1.5 } as const;

  static computeMHDIF(
    referenceResponses: boolean[][], // item scores for reference group
    focalResponses: boolean[][],     // item scores for focal group
    referenceScores: number[],       // total scores for stratification
    focalScores: number[],
  ): {
    alphaMH: number;
    mhDDIF: number;
    category: 'A' | 'B' | 'C';
    direction: 'favors_reference' | 'favors_focal' | 'none';
  } | null {
    if (referenceResponses.length < this.MIN_GROUP_SIZE ||
        focalResponses.length < this.MIN_GROUP_SIZE) {
      return null;
    }
    // Stratify by total score quintiles
    // Compute 2x2 tables per stratum
    // alpha_MH = sum(A*D/T) / sum(B*C/T)
    // MH D-DIF = -2.35 * ln(alpha_MH)
    // Classify by ETS thresholds
  }

  static classifyDIF(mhDDIF: number): 'A' | 'B' | 'C' {
    const abs = Math.abs(mhDDIF);
    if (abs < this.DIF_THRESHOLDS.A) return 'A';
    if (abs <= this.DIF_THRESHOLDS.B) return 'B';
    return 'C';
  }
}
```

## Code patterns to AVOID
```typescript
// ✗ FERPA violation: exposing demographic group values in API response
return { group: 'African American', dif: 1.3 }; // BANNED — only return category

// ✗ Computing DIF on tiny groups — statistically invalid
if (focalGroup.length >= 5) { /* compute */ } // BANNED — must be >= 25

// ✗ Missing stratification — confounds ability with group membership
const alphaMH = (a * d) / (b * c); // BANNED — must stratify by total score
```

```typescript
// tests/E09/E09-S03.api.test.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('MH DIF computed correctly for known textbook example', async () => {
  const { DifService } = await import(
    '../../features/analytics/services/DifService'
  );
  // Holland & Thayer 1988 example data
  const result = DifService.computeMHDIF(
    /* reference responses */, /* focal responses */,
    /* reference scores */, /* focal scores */
  );
  expect(result).not.toBeNull();
  expect(result!.mhDDIF).toBeCloseTo(/* expected value */, 2);
  expect(result!.category).toBe(/* expected category */);
});

test('DIF returns null for groups smaller than 25', async () => {
  const { DifService } = await import(
    '../../features/analytics/services/DifService'
  );
  const result = DifService.computeMHDIF(
    Array(10).fill([true, false]),  // only 10 reference
    Array(30).fill([true, false]),
    Array(10).fill(5),
    Array(30).fill(5),
  );
  expect(result).toBeNull();
});

test('ETS classification thresholds are correct', async () => {
  const { DifService } = await import(
    '../../features/analytics/services/DifService'
  );
  expect(DifService.classifyDIF(0.5)).toBe('A');
  expect(DifService.classifyDIF(1.2)).toBe('B');
  expect(DifService.classifyDIF(2.0)).toBe('C');
  expect(DifService.classifyDIF(-0.5)).toBe('A');
  expect(DifService.classifyDIF(-1.8)).toBe('C');
});

test('API DIF response does not contain demographic group values', async ({ request }) => {
  const { token } = await getTestToken(request, 'faculty');
  const res = await request.get('/api/admin/analytics/items?exam_id=test-exam-id', {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  });
  expect(res.status()).toBe(200);
  const body = await res.text();
  // Ensure no demographic identifiers leak
  expect(body).not.toContain('African American');
  expect(body).not.toContain('ethnicity_value');
});
```
